## Gold

Gold is the only currency, and everything of value can change hands. The economy exists for one reason: war must cost something and peace must be worth something, so trust has a price without any rule saying so.

**Gold.**

- Provinces yield gold each turn; units and characters cost upkeep. From the economy's first phase (build order item 9+a, decided 21 October 2026), provinces produce goods instead, and gold buys labour ("Economy and resources").
- Gold can be paid, promised, lent, withheld or used as a bribe, to any seat or character.
- Gold travels physically with an envoy, so it arrives late and can be skimmed by a greedy carrier.
- **Purity.** A sender may debase a shipment. The receiver sees its face value until it pays for an assay. This recreates the Amarna complaint about Egyptian gold that melted down impure. Once gold is money, markets assay what they are paid ("Markets").
- **Debts are facts; repayment is a choice** (decided 19 October 2026; scoring changed 21 October 2026). A loan is proven by a debt tablet sealed by borrower and lender, recording the sum to be repaid. Nothing forces the borrower to pay, and the score counts what each side holds, not what it owes or is owed: borrowed gold counts as the borrower's, as skimmed gold counts as the skimmer's. Not repaying is a kind of taking, and the world answers it the way it answers theft. The tablet is evidence anyone can read, so the lender's accusation carries where a verbal promise is one man's word against another's; it is a claim that can be sold to someone strong enough to collect; and a known defaulter pays dearly for credit, or finds none. The random ending makes a late default cheaper, so lenders price the end in, and credit grows dearer as the game ages, with no rule setting it. Interest, due dates, collateral and what follows a default stay words. The same tablet works between kings: a king who lends gives up gold until he is repaid. A kingdom's debts die when it falls. Characters lending to kings, and where characters keep their gold, are set out in "Where characters keep their gold" and "Lending to kings".

**Gold is a lifeline** (decided 20 October 2026). For a king, gold is part of how he wins, since it is part of his realm's wealth ("The wealth of a realm" under Victory), and his security: it pays the troops who would otherwise desert, the ransoms and the envoys. For a character it is his security and his own victory, the ranking of the richest. So nobody hands gold out unless he believes it buys a greater benefit on average, over a time he can name: a gift buys favour, a bribe buys a softer report or a secret, a loan buys interest, tribute buys peace. Every request that asks a king or a character to give, take or keep gold says what it is worth to him in those terms, and script kings judge gifts and bribes the same way, as investments with an expected return, rather than by a generosity threshold. The score keeps the same books (decided 21 October 2026): gold a king spends at home stays in his realm, but gold he sends abroad leaves it, so a gift costs him exactly what it gives the receiver and is worth sending only for what it buys.

**Transferable assets.** Provinces, gold, units and characters (including as hostages) can all be given away. Tribute, buffer zones, hostage exchanges and escrow-like deals are left to emerge from these.
